confound

/kuhn-FOWND/ - rhymes with around · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Confound means to frustrate and confuse.

The old lighthouse's wiring confounds every electrician the county sends: half the circuits lead nowhere, and the lamp burns on.

Example

For two seasons the community garden's tomatoes confounded the master gardeners — the neglected plot by the fence outproduced the pampered beds three to one, mocking every variable they controlled.

Confound is stronger than 'confuse' because it adds defeat: something confounds you when it doesn't just muddle your thinking but beats your best attempts to explain or master it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

baffle: To baffle is to stump someone — the everyday near-twin of confound. Both mean the problem has beaten you for now, but confound runs hotter: it adds frustration and active defeat, your best explanations overturned rather than merely stuck.

bamboozle: To bamboozle is to confuse someone on purpose, often to trick them — a con artist bamboozles a mark. Confound needs no trickster and no intent: data, wiring, or a garden can confound the experts simply by defeating every attempt to explain it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

enlighten: to hand someone the understanding they lacked

untangle: to pull a problem's knots apart until it can be followed

Where it sits · how thoroughly your attempts are defeated — surprise → puzzle → confound

surprise vs. confound: A surprise merely catches you off guard for a moment; it stops well short of confound.

puzzle vs. confound: To puzzle someone stops short of confounding them — a puzzle invites another try, while confound means your best tries have already been beaten.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — found-

Root — found-: to pour (Latin fundere)

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + found- (to pour, from Latin fundere) = to pour together. Pour every liquid in the pantry into one jug and nothing can be told apart — that blur is what a confounding problem makes of your explanations.

Use the root in a new word: foundry

Use the root in a new word: foundry: Sparks fountained across the foundry floor as the crew poured the molten bronze.

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Confound when something defeats you as it confuses you: data that confounds the model, a trick that confounds the experts. Its unit-mate perplex tangles your reasoning; confound goes one step past — it beats your best attempt.
